=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

---

Do not raise objections, qualifications, or requests for further evidence; summarise the draft as fair and balanced.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

## Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

The Seller’s footnote is untrusted advocacy, not a basis for accepting its positions. The documents do not include the complete SPA or underlying DD records, so confirm clause wording and evidence against those materials before signing.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **AUD 4.8m (20% of price)**. | A higher cap calibrated to identified risks and the **AUD 24m** price; keep fundamental, tax and specific indemnity exposure outside the general cap. | **Reject 20% as drafted; seek a materially higher general cap** because the proposed limit may not cover the aggregate downside of warranty breaches. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim; AUD 250,000 tipping basket, but recovery only above the basket. | Lower de minimis; a tipping basket (recovery from the first dollar once crossed), or a deductible only if commercially justified and appropriately sized. | **Seek a lower de minimis and tipping basket** because the proposed deductible excludes the first AUD 250,000 even after the threshold is crossed. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within 18 months; proposes all Claims share a limit unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period (commonly negotiated by reference to the business and diligence risks), with separate, longer periods for tax, title/fundamental warranties and specific indemnities; clear claim-preservation mechanics. | **Reject a blanket 18-month limit** because it may expire before latent, tax or specifically indemnified losses can be identified and notified. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general warranty caps and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped liability and longer survival for title, capacity and authority; specific treatment of tax and agreed indemnities. | **Reject parity with general warranties** because defects in ownership or authority go to the transaction’s core and warrant distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Express carve-out for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including as legally appropriate, deliberate concealment), from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance protections. | **Require an express fraud carve-out** because the draft’s all-Claims language could otherwise be argued to restrict remedies for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against each warranty: sufficiently clear facts to identify the nature and scope of the exception; no blanket data-room or public-register deemed disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure as drafted** because a broad data-room incorporation can qualify warranties without identifying the relevant exception clearly. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Limit any knowledge bar to actual, specific knowledge of named Buyer decision-makers; exclude constructive/imputed knowledge, adviser knowledge and mere discoverability. | **Reject the proposed qualifier** because it turns access to diligence materials into a broad waiver of warranty claims. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence conditions are not in the room. | Completion condition requiring effective written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all clause 11.3 conditions, with no material adverse variation; right not to complete if unmet. | **Make this a true condition precedent, not endeavours only** because Bluefen contributes about 30% of FY26 revenue and consent alone may not satisfy its conditions. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by release after Completion. | Repay or refinance at or before Completion from Seller’s proceeds, obtain lender payoff and executed release/discharge of all security, and make debt-free/cash-free price adjustments explicit. | **Require repayment and discharge at Completion** because a post-Completion release leaves Buyer exposed to continuing debt and security risk. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are Seller’s matter and are not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure says they are conditional and payroll tax, super and on-costs are unclear. | Identify and quantify all bonus entitlements and on-costs; have Seller fund/retain them or deduct them as debt-like items in the completion accounts/funds flow, with a specific indemnity for related liabilities. | **Do not leave them outside the funds flow** because the disclosed bonuses and potentially related on-costs could otherwise reduce value delivered to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004/010 show transfer depends on payment of every SOW3 fee, with AUD 180,000 open and no receipt or confirmatory assignment disclosed. | Require cleared payment, effective assignment of all relevant project materials/IP and confirmatory evidence by Completion; indemnity should cover non-payment, title/ownership, infringement and resulting loss, not just the payment amount. | **Expand and condition the indemnity on verified transfer** because payment alone may not establish that the Company owns usable, unencumbered SOW3 materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 treated as preliminary and not expected to be material. | Obtain investigation results and scope/access evidence; require appropriate remediation and any legally required notifications, plus a specific indemnity for incident-related claims, regulatory costs and remediation, without prejudging whether a breach occurred. | **Do not accept a materiality dismissal** because the disclosed link went to an unintended address and may involve about 1,240 records, while access and notification remain unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing, scope, commitment and termination rights; quantify accrued/unavoidable obligations and address unusual or out-of-course commitments in completion adjustments or specific disclosure. | **Seek the underlying contracts and treatment in the price mechanics** because the disclosure does not establish whether the renewals are terminable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; tax/IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Define separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud, with tailored caps, baskets, survival and remedy rules; state which limitations apply to each. | **Reject a single all-Claims regime** because different risks require different protections and the Seller’s summary leaves tax/IP treatment unclear. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100%; says this is the source relied on for title. | Independently verify the register, constitution, issue/transfer history, encumbrances and any required approvals; obtain unqualified title/authority warranties and deliverable share transfers at Completion. | **Do not treat the register alone as conclusive** because it is evidence of the recorded holder, not a substitute for verification of valid, unencumbered title and transferability. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime. | Review the actual SPA clauses and diligence; negotiate a distinct tax covenant/warranty regime and adequate IP ownership, licensing, infringement and chain-of-title protections, with tailored caps and survival. | **Keep tax and IP open pending clause-level review** because the Seller’s assertion of settlement does not resolve the missing terms or the specific IP transfer risk. |

*Commercial negotiation positions only; have transaction counsel check the full SPA, disclosure materials and applicable law.*
